purpose: Removes the disableCoreAutoSizes setting and its wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes blocker, unblocking WordPress 6.7+'s native sizes="auto" feature for lazy-loaded images through the plugin's existing data-sizes pipeline.
riskRationale: Clean surgical removal with no stale references. The plugin's output-buffer-based lazy loading (sizes→data-sizes transformation) correctly preserves core's sizes="auto" addition which happens earlier in the content pipeline. The vendor platform_check.php deletion is the only concern.

text: The core feature change is well-executed: the disableCoreAutoSizes option is fully removed from both PHP (setup_hooks filter) and JS (component default + SwitchField UI) with no stale references anywhere in the codebase. The vendor/autoload_real.php and vendor/platform_check.php changes appear to be an unintended side effect of running composer install --ignore-platform-reqs and are unrelated to the PR's purpose. Build output was regenerated correctly (only index.js + index.asset.php changed).

reasoning: The core feature change is sound and complete, but the unintended removal of vendor/composer/platform_check.php (and the corresponding require in autoload_real.php) must be restored. This is an unrelated side effect that removes the PHP version guard for the entire plugin.

message: Clean surgical removal — the exact 3-line if-block that registered the __return_false filter was removed, with no collateral changes to surrounding code.
Complete removal — both the default value and the entire SwitchField component were removed, with the pre-existing blank-line separator between setting groups preserved for readability.

The existing sizes→data-sizes transformation in process_img_tag correctly preserves core's sizes="auto" by moving it to data-sizes="auto", which the JS lazy loader restores at runtime. This ensures the feature works correctly end-to-end.

The require for platform_check.php was removed from autoload_real.php and the platform_check.php file was deleted entirely. This removes Composer's PHP version guard (≥8.2), causing opaque PHP fatal errors on PHP < 8.2 instead of the clear 'PHP 8.2+ required' message. This is an unintended side effect from running composer install --ignore-platform-reqs during development.
suggestion: Restore vendor/composer/platform_check.php and the require line in vendor/composer/autoload_real.php. Run `composer install` (without --ignore-platform-reqs) to regenerate the file from lock if needed.

purpose: Consolidate duplicated output buffer filesystem guard code between the legacy template_redirect path and the WP 6.9+ template enhancement path, adding a deprecation notice for the legacy path.
riskRationale: Iteration 1 correctly fixed platform_check.php restoration, _doing_it_wrong() scoping, and redundant prepare_cache_dir() removal. However, removing prepare_cache_dir() from save_cache_files() broke the CSS combine path, which calls save_cache_files() directly and silently fails on fresh installs or when HTML caching is disabled.

text: The refactoring of save_processed_buffer() is clean and all three iteration 1 issues have been properly resolved. However, a critical regression was introduced: combine_css() calls save_cache_files() directly, bypassing save_processed_buffer(), and no longer ensures the cache directory exists. This causes silent failures on fresh installs or when HTML caching is disabled.

reasoning: CSS combine path (combine_css() -> save_cache_files()) no longer ensures the cache directory exists, causing silent failures on fresh installs or when HTML caching is disabled. The fix requires a single prepare_cache_dir() call in combine_css() before save_cache_files().

message: save_processed_buffer() cleanly extracts the duplicated get_filesystem() + prepare_cache_dir() guard into a single shared private method — DRY improvement with no behavioral change for the HTML cache paths.
Inline comments clearly disambiguate the WP 6.9+ vs legacy branching for future maintainers.
_doing_it_wrong() properly scoped to defined('WP_DEBUG') && WP_DEBUG && is_admin() — avoids cluttering front-end error logs on every page load.

CSS combine path is broken — save_cache_files() no longer calls prepare_cache_dir() (removed in iteration 1), but combine_css() calls save_cache_files() directly, bypassing save_processed_buffer(). On fresh installs or when HTML caching is disabled, the cache directory won't exist and $fs->put_contents() at line 626 will silently fail.
suggestion: Add a prepare_cache_dir() call in combine_css() before save_cache_files() — only this caller bypasses save_processed_buffer(), so the most targeted fix is to ensure the directory exists in combine_css() itself.

purpose: Replace GD-library-dependent default quality with WP 6.7+ core's wp_image_quality() and rename core_handles_webp() to core_handles_next_gen() for accuracy.
riskRationale: Core PHP logic change is well-guarded by function_exists() and fully backward-compatible. However, manual edits to Composer-generated vendor files (platform_check.php deleted, autoload_real.php require line removed) are fragile — they will be overwritten by any composer command, creating a maintenance hazard since vendor/ is git-tracked.
breakingChanges: Removal of vendor/composer/platform_check.php may break CI workflows that depend on Composer's platform validation

text: The core functionality changes are sound: wp_image_quality() integration with proper fallback and the method rename to core_handles_next_gen() are correctly implemented with all call sites updated. However, the PR contains manual hand-edits to Composer-generated vendor files (autoload_real.php and platform_check.php deletion) that should instead be regenerated via Composer tooling. Two minor code quality issues were also identified in the quality resolution logic.

reasoning: Core PHP changes are correct and well-guarded, but manual edits to Composer-generated vendor files introduce a maintenance liability. The vendor files must be regenerated via Composer tooling before this PR is ready to merge.

message: Renaming core_handles_webp() to core_handles_next_gen() improves accuracy since wp_image_quality() gates support for all next-gen formats (WebP and AVIF), not just WebP.
Using wp_image_quality() (WP 6.7+) for default quality resolves a long-standing TODO of relying on GD library defaults, and the function_exists() guard ensures full backward compatibility.
Fallback value of 82 is a reasonable default when wp_image_quality() is unavailable, matching WordPress core JPEG quality convention.

The require __DIR__ . '/platform_check.php'; line was manually removed from this Composer-generated file, and vendor/composer/platform_check.php was deleted entirely. These files are auto-generated by Composer and will be overwritten by any composer install/update/dump-autoload command. Since vendor/ is git-tracked per project conventions, hand-editing generated files creates a persistent maintenance hazard.
suggestion: Regenerate the autoloader properly by running composer config platform-check false && composer dump-autoload, or run composer release (which runs composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader) as documented in AGENTS.md.
suggestionCode: composer config platform-check false && composer dump-autoload

message: When format is 'both', the MIME is set to 'image/avif', so wp_image_quality('image/avif') resolves the quality. This single value is then used for both WebP and AVIF conversions. WebP and AVIF have different optimal quality ranges, so using an AVIF-derived quality for WebP may produce slightly non-optimal files.
suggestion: Consider resolving separate quality values for each format when format is 'both', or document this as an acceptable simplification since quality values from wp_image_quality() tend to be close across formats.

message: The if/elseif block for MIME type mapping is more verbose than needed — the 'avif' and 'both' cases resolve to the same value.
suggestion: Simplify with a ternary expression using in_array().

message: Comment still says 'skip plugin's own WebP conversion' after renaming the method to core_handles_next_gen(). Since the method now checks for all next-gen formats, the comment should be more precise.
suggestion: Update the comment to reference 'next-gen conversion' instead of just 'WebP conversion', maintaining consistency with the method rename.
suggestionCode: // If WP 6.7+ natively generates next-gen formats, skip plugin's own conversion.

purpose: Add fetchpriority=low to deferred/delayed JS script tags so non-critical scripts don't compete with LCP resources for network priority.
riskRationale: Changes are isolated to script tag rendering. No user input touchpoints, no new data exposure, no architectural changes. The only risk is duplicate fetchpriority attributes on WP 6.9+, which is cosmetic.

text: Well-structured PR that correctly implements fetchpriority=low for deferred and delayed scripts using a two-pronged approach (wp_script_add_data + script_loader_tag fallback). The implementation integrates cleanly with existing defer/delay infrastructure, though two minor opportunities for hardening exist around deduplication and WP 6.9+ compatibility.

message: Good defensive approach — uses both wp_script_add_data('fetchpriority', 'low') for WP 6.9+ native support AND a script_loader_tag fallback for backward compatibility. The priority 11 on the fallback ensures it runs after add_defer_attribute().
Correct str_replace ordering: fetchpriority is inserted before the wppo-src rewrite, so both attributes appear properly on delayed script tags.
Proper integration with existing exclusion lists — handles in $exclude_defer_js are correctly skipped from both defer and fetchpriority.
$deferred_handles uses a flat array, so the same handle could be appended multiple times if add_defer_strategy() runs more than once, and in_array() on the fallback filter is O(n) per script tag.
suggestion: Use an associative array keyed by handle name for O(1) lookups and automatic deduplication.

message: If WP 6.9 natively supports fetchpriority via wp_script_add_data, the script_loader_tag fallback will add a duplicate attribute (e.g. fetchpriority="low" fetchpriority="low") because str_replace operates on the already-rendered tag. Harmless but wasteful.
suggestion: Check if the tag already contains fetchpriority before inserting, or gate the fallback filter behind a WP version check (e.g. only register the filter when WP < 6.9).

purpose: Add wp_cache_supports('flush_group') feature detection to Cache::flush_group() and attempt to register flush_group support in the Redis object-cache drop-in.
riskRationale: The class-cache.php change is correct and safe. The object-cache.php change is dead code that has no runtime effect, but should be cleaned up before merge.

text: The class-cache.php change correctly gates flush_group on wp_cache_supports('flush_group') with proper backward-compatible fallback. The object-cache.php change attempts to use wp_cache_supports() as a registration function, but it is a read-only query function — the two-argument call is a no-op and should be removed.

reasoning: The object-cache.php lines 938-940 are dead code that misuses the wp_cache_supports() API. The feature detection already works automatically because WP_Object_Cache has a flush_group() method. Remove the spurious call.

message: The flush_group() method correctly uses wp_cache_supports('flush_group') as the primary guard with a function_exists() check for backward compatibility, and preserves the legacy function_exists + method_exists fallback for WP < 6.1.
The early return via wp_cache_supports() is the idiomatic WP 6.1+ approach and aligns with core best practices for cache backend capability detection.

wp_cache_supports() is a read-only query function defined with a single $feature parameter — the second argument true is silently ignored. This call does not register flush_group support. Since WP_Object_Cache already implements flush_group() (line 572), wp_cache_supports('flush_group') will correctly return true after wp_cache_init() without any special registration. These three lines are dead code.
suggestion: Remove the entire if block at lines 938-940. No registration is needed — the drop-in self-advertises flush_group support automatically via the method on WP_Object_Cache.

message: Using wp_cache_supports() as a setter is a misunderstanding of the API. This is a query-only function that returns a boolean based on the cache backend's capabilities.
suggestion: Remove this line along with the surrounding if block.
